title: Animals Living in Groups
seo_title: Grade 3 Animal Groups Worksheets: How Living in Groups Helps Animals Survive
standard_text: Construct an argument that some animals form groups that help members survive.
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets on animals living in groups (NGSS 3-LS2-1): packs, herds, schools and colonies, how groups help animals get food, stay safe and survive, with hunting data. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: Living in a group helps some animals survive.
key_sub: Groups help animals get food, stay safe, survive changes and share jobs.
body_html:
How to think about it

Some animals live in groups. Being in a group can help each member survive:

  • Getting food: wolves and lions hunt together to catch big prey.
  • Staying safe: fish swim in schools, zebras stay in herds and meerkats take turns as lookouts.
  • Surviving changes: penguins huddle in the cold; elephants lead the herd to water in dry seasons.
  • Dividing jobs: ants and bees share the work in a colony.

Not all animals live in groups. Tigers and bears mostly live alone.

Example

How does hunting in a pack help wolves?

One wolf cannot catch a deer alone.

A pack can.

Answer: They catch bigger prey and get more food.

Example

Why do fish swim in schools?

A predator cannot pick one fish out of a big group.

Answer: to stay safe

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all animals live in groups.
  • Thinking groups help only the leader. Groups help many members.
  • Forgetting that group members also share or compete for food.

faq.q: Why do some animals live in groups?
faq.a: Groups help them catch food, stay safe from predators, survive cold or dry seasons, and share jobs.

faq.q: Do all animals live in groups?
faq.a: No. Some animals, like tigers and bears, mostly live alone.

faq.q: How do bees and ants work together?
faq.a: They divide jobs. Some find food, some care for the young and some guard the nest, so the whole colony survives.

items.q: What is a group of ants called?
items.e: A group of ants is called a colony.

items.q: In a beehive, why does each bee have a job?
c: Splitting up jobs helps the whole colony survive.
items.e: Workers, guards and the queen all help.

items.q: Nora reads that fish swim close together. How does living in a group mostly help them?
items.e: It is hard for a predator to pick out one fish from a big, moving group.
